hero.lead: A nation of 19.9 million between the Andes and the Pacific, where minerals earn a sixth of the economy and the Treasury sold €3.1 billion of euro bonds in July 2026.

register.name: Swiss franc bonds, two tranches
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · 28 September 2026 · CHF 210M due 2031 at 1.5275% · CHF 170M due 2036 at 1.865%
register.note: Chile’s first sovereign issuance in Swiss francs, equivalent to US$458 million
register.text: Chile’s first sovereign bonds denominated in Swiss francs: a five-year bond of CHF 210 million and a ten-year bond of CHF 170 million, equivalent to US$458 million in all. The placement is part of the 2026 financing plan and widens the Republic’s sources of funding and its base of investors.

register.name: Euro bonds, three tranches
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · 27 July 2026 · €1.25bn due 2034 at 4.101% · €1.1bn due 2038 at 4.424% · €750M due 2046 at 4.759%
register.note: The first international placement under Law 21,831; orders of €8.7 billion, 2.8 times the amount placed
register.text: Three euro bonds of eight, twelve and twenty years, the first international placement under Law 21,831, which authorises up to US$6.2 billion of additional central government borrowing in 2026. Orders reached €8.7 billion, 2.8 times the amount placed.

register.name: Bond issuance programme, 2026
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · updated financing plan, 10 July 2026 · local market US$14bn (60%) · external markets US$9.6bn (40%)
register.note: Raised from US$17.4 billion; about US$4.4 billion of external bonds already issued in January
register.text: The Ministry of Finance raised its bond issuance programme for 2026 to US$23.6 billion, from US$17.4 billion, in line with a bill passed by Congress that authorises additional borrowing of up to US$6.2 billion. Sixty per cent is to be issued in the local market and forty per cent in external markets.

register.name: Euro and dollar bonds, with a sustainability-linked bond
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · 7 January 2026 · US$850M due 2031 at 4.372% · €1.5bn due 2032 at 3.460% · €1.5bn sustainability-linked due 2036 at 3.928%
register.note: The sustainability-linked bond lowers its interest rate if biodiversity targets are met by 2030
register.text: Bonds equivalent to US$4,375 million: US$850 million due 2031, €1.5 billion due 2032 and a €1.5 billion sustainability-linked bond due 2036. The sustainability-linked bond, a first for Chile, carries a step-down in its interest rate if at least 30% of Chile’s land territory is protected and at least 10% meets criteria of protection and effective management by 2030.

register.name: Flexible Credit Line
register.detail: IMF · Central Bank of Chile · 26 August 2026 · two years · SDR 8,721.5M
register.note: Precautionary; the Central Bank has never drawn on the line
register.text: A precautionary and temporary IMF credit line held by the Central Bank of Chile, renewed by the IMF Executive Board for two more years with access reduced to US$11.8 billion (SDR 8,721.5 million). It replaces the line of August 2024; the Central Bank has never used it.

register.name: Cross-sectoral social protection
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 22 May 2025 · Ministry of Social Development and Family · Ministry of Women and Gender Equality
register.note: To make social protection more inclusive, effective and efficient
register.text: A World Bank loan to improve the quality of cross-sectoral social protection in Chile, implemented by the Ministry of Social Development and Family and the Ministry of Women and Gender Equality. One of its areas covers persons with different levels of dependency and unpaid caregivers, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Chile’s Water Transition
register.note: To strengthen Chile’s capacity for water resource management and water-related services
register.text: A Program-for-Results loan of US$250 million to strengthen the capacity of Chile for water resource management and water-related services. It serves the water standard.

register.name: Program for Universal Primary Healthcare Coverage and Resilience
register.note: Primary care, telemedicine and rural clinics
register.text: A World Bank loan to support Chile’s universal primary care programme and improve the population’s access to quality health services. It expands access to primary care, including telemedicine and rural clinics, prepares the health system for climate change and public health emergencies, and improves efficiency and transparency through a virtual platform for managing demand.

register.name: REDD-plus results-based payments, 2014–2016
register.detail: Green Climate Fund · FAO · Approved 14 November 2019 · completion date 7 August 2026
register.note: Results-based payment, reinvested in the National Strategy on Climate Change and Vegetation Resources
register.text: A results-based payment of US$63,607,552 from the Green Climate Fund for Chile’s reduced emissions from deforestation and forest degradation in the results period 2014 to 2016, with FAO as the accredited entity. The payment is reinvested to deepen Chile’s National Strategy on Climate Change and Vegetation Resources.

register.name: Housing finance loan to Banco Consorcio
register.note: Chile’s housing shortfall is put at 927,000 homes, 14% of households
register.text: An IFC loan to Banco Consorcio to expand access to housing finance in Chile and enable more women to obtain mortgage loans. The release puts the housing shortfall at 927,000 homes, equal to 14% of households; the loan serves the shelter standard.

items.alt: A tree-lined street in Santiago with the Andes behind and people in the distance, Chile

items.name: Conectado Aprendo
items.text: An organisation that tackles learning lag with personalised one-to-one online tutoring and continuous monitoring, bringing families and schools together to level learning and strengthen social and emotional skills. It won the education category of Chile’s Avonni national innovation awards in October 2025.

items.name: Fundación Reimagina
items.text: A Chilean foundation working to close education gaps in Latin America, where half of 15-year-olds struggle with basic reading; over 1.2 million teachers in the region have received its professional development, and Chile, Ecuador and Paraguay have incorporated its methods into national policy. It was a finalist for the Schwab Foundation social innovation awards of 2026.

items.name: Lirmi
items.text: A school platform founded in La Araucanía that brings planning, assessment and real-time data analysis together for teachers, with more than 2,700 schools in Latin America and 4 million users. In 2025 it renewed its alliance with Enseña Chile, whose teachers use the platform free of charge.

items.name: TECHO-Chile
items.text: An organisation that builds transitional homes for families in extreme vulnerability who lack basic services, while they move towards a definitive home. In 2025 it completed one in El Monte, in the Metropolitan Region, the first of two planned that year with Porsche in Chile.

items.name: ÑAM (Fundación Gastronomía Social)
items.text: A gastronomy platform that combines hybrid training, access to employment and motivational tools to tackle unemployment, informality and youth mental health, in a country where close to a million young people face barriers to work. It won the social innovation category of Chile’s Avonni national innovation awards in October 2025.
